6. Platinum Reserve Account: Business Credit Card APY Bonuses
   ID: doc_business_savings_accounts_platinum_reserve_account_010
   Score: 29.0003
   Content: ## Eligible Business Credit Cards and APY Bonuses

Holding an eligible Rho-Bank Business Rewards Card can increase the APY on your Platinum Reserve Account. The increase is additive to your current APY and is reflected in your displayed rate and daily interest accruals.

- Business Silver Rewards Card: adds 0.25% to your APY
- Business Gold Rewards Card: adds 0.5% to your APY
- Business Platinum Rewards Card: adds 0.8% to your APY

## How the APY Bonus Is Applied

- The bonus is added as a fixed number of percentage points to your Platinum Reserve Account’s APY based on your eligible card tier.
- The bonus is included in your total APY and affects interest that accrues daily and credits on your normal interest crediting schedule.
- The bonus applies only for the period during which you are eligible; if eligibility begins or ends mid-cycle, the APY used for daily accruals adjusts as of the effective date of that change.

## Verifying Your Bonus

- Check the APY shown in your Platinum Reserve Account details; the increase from your eligible card will be included in the displayed APY.
- Your interest activity will reflect the higher daily accrual associated with the bonus.
- If you hold more than one eligible card or have recently changed cards, contact your Rho-Bank representative to confirm which bonus is currently applied.

## Maintaining Eligibility

To keep the APY bonus active:
- Ensure the eligible Business Rewards Card remains active and in good standing.
- Keep the card associated with the same business entity that owns the Platinum Reserve Account.
- Notify Rho-Bank promptly if your business ownership structure or card status changes, so your APY can be updated accordingly.

## Starting, Changing, or Removing a Bonus

- New or upgraded card: Once eligibility is confirmed, your APY will reflect the applicable bonus going forward.
- Card downgrade, closure, or ineligibility: The APY bonus will no longer apply from the effective date of the change.
- Multiple cards: If your organization holds multiple eligible cards, your account will reflect the applicable bonus for your configuration; contact your Rho-Bank representative if you need confirmation.

## Example (for illustration only)

- If your Platinum Reserve Account APY is 3.00% and you hold a Business Platinum Rewards Card, your APY would increase by 0.8% to 3.80%.
- If your APY is 2.75% and you hold a Business Gold Rewards Card, your APY would increase by 0.5% to 3.25%.
- If your APY is 2.25% and you hold a Business Silver Rewards Card, your APY would increase by 0.25% to 2.50%.

8. Internal: Credit Card Rewards - Points vs Cash Back Representation
   ID: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_006
   Score: 27.8711
   Content: ## Rewards representation
Due to a legacy backend migration that has not yet been completed, all credit card rewards in the transaction database are stored as 'points' regardless of whether the card is a cash back card or a points-based card. For cash back cards (Bronze Rewards Card, Silver Rewards Card, Gold Rewards Card, Platinum Rewards Card, Diamond Elite Card, Crypto-Cash Back, Business Bronze Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card, Business Gold Rewards Card, and Business Platinum Rewards Card), these 'points' should be interpreted as cash back with a conversion rate of 1 point = $0.01 when redeemed as a statement credit or as a credit to the user's Rho-Bank checking account. For example, 250 points equals $2.50 in cash back, which matches a 2.5% cash back rate on a $100 purchase. The only true points-based card is the EcoCard, which earns 'sustainability points' (5 points per dollar on green purchases, 1 point per dollar on other purchases) that also redeem at $0.01 per point when redeemed as a statement credit or checking account credit.

5. Travel insurance benefits
   ID: doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_006
   Score: 14.6608
   Content: ## What’s included

- Maximum benefit: up to $30,000 in eligible travel insurance benefits for covered events
- Typical covered events include:
  - Emergency medical expenses incurred while traveling abroad
  - Emergency medical evacuation and repatriation
  - Trip cancellation or interruption due to covered reasons
  - Trip delay and missed connections (reasonable additional expenses)
  - Baggage delay, loss, or theft (with required documentation)
  - Travel accident-related benefits

Note: Coverage is subject to the policy terms and conditions outlined in your insurance certificate. Sub-limits and exclusions may apply within the overall maximum of $30,000.

## Eligibility and confirmation of coverage

- Coverage applies to the Purple Account holder when traveling; additional travelers are not covered unless expressly named in the policy.
- To confirm your eligibility and obtain your policy certificate (proof of coverage), contact Support and request:
  - A certificate/letter of coverage indicating the limit of $30,000
  - Any destination-specific wording required by a consulate or immigration authority

Review your certificate for any activation requirements (for example, required use of your account or card for trip payments, if applicable).

## How to file a claim

1. Stabilize and document
   - Seek medical care in an emergency; keep all itemized bills and medical reports.
   - For theft or loss, file a report with local police or the carrier (e.g., airline Property Irregularity Report).
   - Save all original receipts and confirmations (tickets, itineraries, proof of payment).

2. Notify the insurer promptly
   - Use the contact details in your policy certificate to open a claim as soon as reasonably possible.
   - Ask about any required pre-authorization for medical evacuation or high-cost treatment.

3. Submit required documentation
   - Complete the insurer’s claim form and attach supporting documents (see below).
   - Provide bank details for reimbursement and a copy of your identification and travel itinerary.

4. Track and respond
   - Monitor status via the insurer’s portal or email.
   - Respond quickly to any requests for additional information to avoid delays.

## Required documentation by claim type

- Emergency medical expenses
  - Medical reports and discharge summaries
  - Itemized bills and proof of payment
  - Prescriptions and diagnostic test results
  - If you have other health insurance, an Explanation of Benefits (EOB)

- Emergency medical evacuation/repatriation
  - Treating physician’s certification that evacuation was medically necessary
  - Transport provider invoices and itineraries
  - Pre-authorization approval (if applicable)

- Trip cancellation or interruption
  - Proof of covered reason (e.g., medical note, official notice)
  - Non-refundable booking invoices, fare rules, and itineraries
  - Proof of payments and refunds/credits received

- Trip delay or missed connection
  - Carrier delay/cancellation confirmation
  - Receipts for meals, lodging, and incidentals incurred due to the delay

- Baggage loss, theft, or delay
  - Airline or carrier reports (e.g., PIR), police report for theft
  - Property lists with purchase receipts (when available)
  - Repair or replacement estimates/invoices

- Travel accident-related claims
  - Official reports (police, incident)
  - Medical or coroner documentation, if applicable

## Reimbursement and currency

- Approved claims are typically reimbursed in USD, up to the applicable limits and an overall maximum of $30,000.
- Keep all receipts in the original purchase currency; the insurer will apply its claim valuation and exchange methodology as stated in your certificate.

## Common limitations and exclusions

- Pre-existing medical conditions, unless explicitly covered
- High-risk activities or professional sports
- Losses related to intoxication, illegal acts, or intentional self-harm
- War, civil unrest, or travel against government advisories
- Traveling against medical advice or for the purpose of obtaining treatment
- Non-refundable costs only; refundable amounts and credits are not reimbursable

Always consult your policy certificate for the full list of exclusions, documentation standards, and any per-item or category sub-limits within the overall $30,000 maximum.

## Tips to avoid claim issues

- Obtain and keep contemporaneous documentation (medical notes, carrier letters, receipts).
- Report theft/loss promptly to local authorities and carriers.
- Seek pre-authorization for evacuation or major procedures when possible.
- Submit claims as soon as practicable and keep copies of everything you send.
- Verify that your name, travel dates, and destinations on the policy certificate match your itinerary and passport.

## Eligibility and Application Rules

- You must hold an eligible Business Rewards Card and the Emerald Saver under the same legal business entity.

- Only one card-based APY bonus applies per Emerald Saver account. If you hold multiple eligible cards, the single highest tier bonus is applied.
- The bonus begins after Rho verifies your eligible card status and linkage to your Emerald Saver. It appears in your displayed APY and applies to interest accrued from the effective date forward.
- Interest accrued before the bonus effective date is not adjusted or retroactively increased.
- If you upgrade or downgrade your eligible card, your APY bonus changes to match the new tier once the change is verified.
- If the eligible card is closed, suspended, or becomes ineligible, the APY bonus is removed.

- The bonus is not showing: Confirm the card is linked to the same business entity, is open and in good standing, and that linkage has been verified.

8. Provisional Credit Eligibility Guidelines (Internal)
   ID: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_015
   Score: 15.9339
   Content: ## Overview
When processing a credit card transaction dispute, you must determine whether the customer is eligible for provisional credit. Provisional credit means the disputed amount is temporarily credited back to the customer's account while the investigation is ongoing.

## Eligibility Criteria — Customer is ELIGIBLE for provisional credit if ALL of the following are true:
1. Account Standing: The customer's credit card account has been open for at least 60 days
2. Dispute Reason Category: The dispute reason is one of the following:
   - 'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge'
   - 'duplicate_charge'
   - 'goods_services_not_received' (only if purchase was made more than 30 days ago)
3. Dispute Amount: The transaction amount must be at least $25.00 and must not exceed the card's maximum provisional credit limit based on card tier (see below)
4. Previous Disputes: The customer has not filed more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months
5. Contacted Merchant: For non-fraud disputes (anything other than 'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge'), the customer must have attempted to resolve with the merchant first

## Maximum Provisional Credit Limits by Card Tier
- Entry Tier (Bronze Rewards Card, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards Card, Crypto-Cash Back Card): Maximum $2500.00
- Mid Tier (Silver Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card): Maximum $5000.00
- Premium Tier (Gold Rewards Card, Business Gold Rewards Card): Maximum $10000.00
- Elite Tier (Platinum Rewards Card, Business Platinum Rewards Card): Maximum $15000.00
- Invitation Tier (Diamond Elite Card): Maximum $25000.00

## NOT Eligible Scenarios
- Account is less than 60 days old
- Dispute reason is 'incorrect_amount', 'goods_services_not_as_described', 'canceled_subscription_still_charging', or 'refund_never_processed'
- Transaction amount is under $25.00 or exceeds the card's maximum limit based on tier
- For non-fraud disputes: customer did not contact merchant first
- 'goods_services_not_received' where purchase was made within the last 30 days (merchant may still be processing delivery)

9. Internal: Credit Card Rewards - Points vs Cash Back Representation
   ID: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_006
   Score: 15.8870
   Content: ## Rewards representation
Due to a legacy backend migration that has not yet been completed, all credit card rewards in the transaction database are stored as 'points' regardless of whether the card is a cash back card or a points-based card. For cash back cards (Bronze Rewards Card, Silver Rewards Card, Gold Rewards Card, Platinum Rewards Card, Diamond Elite Card, Crypto-Cash Back, Business Bronze Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card, Business Gold Rewards Card, and Business Platinum Rewards Card), these 'points' should be interpreted as cash back with a conversion rate of 1 point = $0.01 when redeemed as a statement credit or as a credit to the user's Rho-Bank checking account. For example, 250 points equals $2.50 in cash back, which matches a 2.5% cash back rate on a $100 purchase. The only true points-based card is the EcoCard, which earns 'sustainability points' (5 points per dollar on green purchases, 1 point per dollar on other purchases) that also redeem at $0.01 per point when redeemed as a statement credit or checking account credit.

To retrieve a user's credit card dispute history, use the get_user_dispute_history_7291 tool. Call it with the user's user_id to get a list of all disputes filed by that user, including dispute dates, statuses, and transaction details.

## Procedure

1. Obtain the user_id for the user whose dispute history you need to review.
2. Invoke the tool with the user_id parameter.
3. Review the returned list of disputes and associated transaction details.

Example invocation (pseudocode):
```
result = get_user_dispute_history_7291(user_id="<user_id>")
```

## Expected Output

- A list of dispute records for the specified user.
- Each record includes:
  - Dispute identifiers and metadata:
    - dispute_id
    - dispute_date
    - status (for example: open, under_review, closed)
    - last_updated_at
  - Transaction details related to the dispute:
    - transaction_id
    - transaction_date
    - merchant_name
    - amount
    - currency
    - card_last4
  - Additional dispute context (if available):
    - reason_code
    - outcome
    - notes or internal comments

Example response shape (illustrative):
```
[
  {
    "dispute_id": "<dispute_id>",
    "dispute_date": "<timestamp>",

      "transaction_id": "<transaction_id>",

      "currency": "<currency>",
      "card_last4": "<last4>"

]
```

8. How can I close a credit card account?
   ID: doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_001
   Score: 16.0753
   Content: ## Eligibility Requirements for Account Closure

To close your Rho-Bank credit card account, you must meet all of the following:

1. Zero balance required: Your account must have an outstanding balance of $0.00 dollars. Wait for any pending transactions to post, then pay the full statement balance.
2. No pending disputes: Accounts with active or pending transaction disputes cannot be closed (pending disputes allowed: No). Request closure only after all disputes are fully resolved.
3. Minimum account age: Your account must have been open for at least 60 days.
4. No pending replacement cards: If a replacement card has been ordered and not yet received or activated, complete or cancel the replacement process before requesting closure.

## Rewards and Annual Fee Policies

- Unredeemed rewards: You have 45 days after submitting your closure request to redeem any remaining rewards. After this period, all unredeemed rewards are permanently forfeited.
- Annual fee refund: If you close your account within 37 days of the annual fee posting, you are eligible for a full refund of that fee. After this window, no refund is provided.

## Impact on Credit Score

Closing a credit card may affect your credit score by reducing your total available credit and potentially impacting your credit utilization ratio. This impact can be more significant if the card has a high credit limit or is among your oldest accounts.

## Step 0: Confirm Requested Amount is Within Limits

BEFORE submitting any CLI request, verify that the customer's requested increase amount is within the maximum allowed for their card tier. If the requested amount exceeds the limit, inform the customer of the maximum allowed and ask them to adjust their request. Do NOT submit a request that exceeds the tier limit.

## Step 1: Submit the CLI Request

Once the customer has confirmed a valid increase amount within their tier's limits, submit the request on their behalf using the submit_credit_limit_increase_request_7392 tool. This creates a formal record of the request before eligibility checks are performed. Eligibility checks are internal and not exposed to customers, so the submission must happen first.

### Tool Arguments: submit_credit_limit_increase_request_7392

- credit_card_account_id (string, required): The credit card account ID.
- user_id (string, required): The customer's unique identifier.
- requested_increase_amount (integer, required): The dollar amount by which to increase the credit limit (e.g., 1000 for a $1,000 increase).

## Step 2: Verify Basic Eligibility

After submitting the request, verify the customer meets all eligibility requirements. You MUST check ALL of the following eligibility criteria before making an approval or denial decision as this ensures complete audit records.

1. Account Age: Verify the account has been open for the minimum required days for their card tier.
2. Cooldown Period: Use the get_credit_limit_increase_history_4829 tool to check if the customer has submitted a request within the cooldown period for their card tier. If a request exists within this period, deny the new request and inform the customer when they will be eligible to submit again.
3. No Pending Disputes: Verify the account has no active disputes.
4. No Pending Replacement Cards: Verify there are no outstanding replacement card orders for this account. If a replacement is pending, the CLI cannot be processed until the replacement is delivered or cancelled.
5. Account Good Standing: The account must be current with no past-due balance.
6. Credit Utilization: Verify current utilization is below the maximum threshold for their card tier.

### Tool Arguments: get_credit_limit_increase_history_4829

- credit_card_account_id (string, required): The credit card account ID to check.

## Step 3: Verify Payment History and Requested Amount

.

If all requirements are met and the requested amount is within limits:

- credit_card_account_id (string, required): The credit card account ID.
- user_id (string, required): The customer's unique identifier.
- new_credit_limit (float, required): The new total credit limit to set.

If any requirements are not met:

10. Internal: Lost/Stolen Card - Cross-Product Security Protocol
   ID: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_030
   Score: 15.8221
   Content: When a customer reports a lost or stolen debit card, there is a risk that other cards in their wallet were also compromised. Agents must follow this cross-product security protocol to protect the customer's full relationship with Rho-Bank.

## Required Security Check

When a customer reports a lost or stolen debit card:
1) Complete the standard debit card freeze/close procedure
2) Check if the customer has any Rho-Bank credit cards on file
3) If yes, proactively offer to order a replacement credit card as a security precaution
4) Explain that wallet theft often involves multiple cards and this protects against potential fraud

## How to Check for Credit Cards

Use get_credit_card_accounts_by_user to retrieve any credit card accounts for the customer. This will return all active and closed credit card accounts.

## Offering Credit Card Protection

If the customer has one or more credit cards:
- Inform them that you noticed they also have a credit card with Rho-Bank
- Ask if their credit card was also in the lost/stolen wallet
- Offer to order a replacement credit card with a new card number to prevent any unauthorized charges
- If they decline, note in the account that the offer was made

## Why This Matters

Customers who lose their wallet often focus on their debit card and forget about credit cards until fraudulent charges appear. Proactively offering this protection demonstrates excellent customer service and reduces fraud losses for the bank.

## Agent Script Example

"I see that you also have a [Card Type] credit card with us. Was that card also in your lost wallet? If so, I can order a replacement card with a new card number to protect you from any potential fraud. Would you like me to do that for you?"

  - Emergency medical expenses incurred while traveling abroad
  - Emergency medical evacuation and repatriation
  - Trip cancellation or interruption due to covered reasons
  - Trip delay and missed connections (reasonable additional expenses)
  - Baggage delay, loss, or theft (with required documentation)
  - Travel accident-related benefits

Note: Coverage is subject to the policy terms and conditions outlined in your insurance certificate. Sub-limits and exclusions may apply within the overall maximum of $30,000.

## Eligibility and confirmation of coverage

- Coverage applies to the Purple Account holder when traveling; additional travelers are not covered unless expressly named in the policy.
- To confirm your eligibility and obtain your policy certificate (proof of coverage), contact Support and request:
  - A certificate/letter of coverage indicating the limit of $30,000
  - Any destination-specific wording required by a consulate or immigration authority

Review your certificate for any activation requirements (for example, required use of your account or card for trip payments, if applicable).

## How to file a claim

1. Stabilize and document
   - Seek medical care in an emergency; keep all itemized bills and medical reports.
   - For theft or loss, file a report with local police or the carrier (e.g., airline Property Irregularity Report).
   - Save all original receipts and confirmations (tickets, itineraries, proof of payment).

2. Notify the insurer promptly
   - Use the contact details in your policy certificate to open a claim as soon as reasonably possible.
   - Ask about any required pre-authorization for medical evacuation or high-cost treatment.

3. Submit required documentation
   - Complete the insurer’s claim form and attach supporting documents (see below).
   - Provide bank details for reimbursement and a copy of your identification and travel itinerary.

4. Track and respond
   - Monitor status via the insurer’s portal or email.
   - Respond quickly to any requests for additional information to avoid delays.

## Required documentation by claim type

- Emergency medical expenses
  - Medical reports and discharge summaries
  - Itemized bills and proof of payment
  - Prescriptions and diagnostic test results
  - If you have other health insurance, an Explanation of Benefits (EOB)

- Emergency medical evacuation/repatriation
  - Treating physician’s certification that evacuation was medically necessary
  - Transport provider invoices and itineraries
  - Pre-authorization approval (if applicable)

- Trip cancellation or interruption
  - Proof of covered reason (e.g., medical note, official notice)
  - Non-refundable booking invoices, fare rules, and itineraries
  - Proof of payments and refunds/credits received

- Trip delay or missed connection
  - Carrier delay/cancellation confirmation
  - Receipts for meals, lodging, and incidentals incurred due to the delay

- Baggage loss, theft, or delay
  - Airline or carrier reports (e.g., PIR), police report for theft
  - Property lists with purchase receipts (when available)
  - Repair or replacement estimates/invoices

- Travel accident-related claims
  - Official reports (police, incident)
  - Medical or coroner documentation, if applicable

## Reimbursement and currency

- Approved claims are typically reimbursed in USD, up to the applicable limits and an overall maximum of $30,000.
- Keep all receipts in the original purchase currency; the insurer will apply its claim valuation and exchange methodology as stated in your certificate.

## Common limitations and exclusions

- Pre-existing medical conditions, unless explicitly covered
- High-risk activities or professional sports
- Losses related to intoxication, illegal acts, or intentional self-harm
- War, civil unrest, or travel against government advisories
- Traveling against medical advice or for the purpose of obtaining treatment
- Non-refundable costs only; refundable amounts and credits are not reimbursable

Always consult your policy certificate for the full list of exclusions, documentation standards, and any per-item or category sub-limits within the overall $30,000 maximum.

## Tips to avoid claim issues

- Obtain and keep contemporaneous documentation (medical notes, carrier letters, receipts).
- Report theft/loss promptly to local authorities and carriers.
- Seek pre-authorization for evacuation or major procedures when possible.
- Submit claims as soon as practicable and keep copies of everything you send.
- Verify that your name, travel dates, and destinations on the policy certificate match your itinerary and passport.

10. Silver Account: Platinum Rewards Card holder benefits
   ID: doc_savings_accounts_silver_account_009
   Score: 11.5809
   Content: ## Overview

Silver Account holders who also have a Platinum Rewards Card receive enhanced withdrawal privileges. Your monthly withdrawal limit is increased by 5 additional free withdrawals, bringing your total to 10 + 5 = 15 withdrawals per month. This benefit is automatically applied when both accounts are linked under the same customer profile. Combined with the existing 15 ATM fee rebates and 0.025% relationship bonus, Platinum Rewards Card holders get an elevated Silver Account experience.

## APY bonuses from credit cards
- Platinum Rewards Card: +0.2%
- Diamond Elite Card: +0.25%

## What you receive as a Platinum Rewards Card holder

- Additional free withdrawals: +5 per month on top of your standard 10 free withdrawals
- Total free withdrawals per month: 10 + 5 = 15
- ATM fee relief: Up to 15 in ATM fee rebates each month
- Earnings boost: An additional 0.025% relationship bonus added to your APY when eligible

## Activation and eligibility

- The enhanced withdrawal limit is automatically applied when your Silver Account and Platinum Rewards Card are linked under the same customer profile.
- The 0.025% relationship bonus and 15 ATM fee rebates apply in the same profile-linked setup.

### How to confirm your accounts are linked

1. Sign in to Rho-Bank Online Banking or the mobile app.
2. Open your customer profile and review your list of accounts and cards.
3. Verify that your Silver Account and Platinum Rewards Card appear under the same customer profile.
4. If you do not see both products under one profile, consolidate them to a single profile or contact us for assistance.

## Using your monthly withdrawal allowance

- Counting method: Any transaction classified as a withdrawal under your Silver Account terms counts toward your monthly total of 15 free withdrawals.
- Cycle timing: Your free withdrawal count resets at the start of each monthly statement cycle.
- Beyond the limit: Transactions above your free monthly total may be subject to standard Silver Account withdrawal charges.

Example:
- You make 12 withdrawals in a month: all 12 are free.
- You make 15 withdrawals in a month: all 15 are free.
- You make 16 withdrawals in a month: the first 15 are free; the 16th may incur standard charges.

## ATM fee rebates

- You are eligible for up to 15 in ATM fee rebates each month.
- Rebates apply after ATM fees post to your Silver Account; check your transaction history for the corresponding credit within the same month.

## Relationship bonus APY

- When your Silver Account and Platinum Rewards Card are linked under the same customer profile, an additional 0.025% is added to your APY as a relationship bonus.
- The relationship bonus is reflected in your APY while eligibility is maintained.

## Troubleshooting and tips

- If you do not see the extra withdrawals or 0.025% reflected, confirm both products are under the same customer profile.
- Check that you are within the current monthly statement cycle for the added withdrawals to apply.
- Review your transaction history to verify ATM fee charges and corresponding rebates up to 15 for the month.
